request.spec:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Draft claims can now be deleted and restored, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How it behaves:**
- **Delete:** a new Delete button on each claim. It works only on a DRAFT that isn't in a closed period; anything else shows the claim's error and changes nothing. The claim's status becomes DELETED, its log gets a `DELETED` line, and `CLAIM_DELETED` is written to the audit file with the person, amount and date.
- **Restore:** a new Restore button turns a DELETED claim back into a DRAFT, but only on the sheet-today it was deleted. That date comes from the last `DELETED` line in the claim's log. It adds a `DRAFT` log line and writes `CLAIM_RESTORED`; on a later day it is refused.
- **Counting:** a deleted claim isn't in any total. It isn't in the header or summary status counts either, because those only list the five existing statuses.
- **Blocked actions:** a deleted claim can't be edited, opened or voided. Those actions only accept specific statuses, and DELETED isn't one of them.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V65__claim_deleted.sql`, adds `DELETED` to the allowed claim statuses.
- **Server:** `ClaimStatus` has the new `DELETED` status. `ClaimService` has `delete` and `restore`, and `ClaimController` has the matching `/claims/{id}/delete` and `/claims/{id}/restore` endpoints.
- **Front end:** in `claims.ts`, the claim types include the new status and actions, and the two buttons use `data-testid="claim-delete"` and `"claim-restore"`.

**One thing I left alone:** a deleted claim can still take a proof or a comment. The request didn't mention either, so I didn't block them. Say if you want them refused.
